chunks: And Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام said:

There is no servant from among our Shiʿah who stands for salat (prayer) except that angels, equal in number to those who oppose him, surround him, praying behind him and supplicating to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, for him until he finishes his salat (prayer).

key_terms.اكْتَنَفَتْهُ: surround him; encompass him from all sides
key_terms.الصَّلَاةِ: salat (prayer); the prescribed act of worship
key_terms.شِيعَتِنَا: our Shiʿah; the followers and adherents of the Ahl al-Bayt عليهم السلام
key_terms.صَلَاتِهِ: his salat (prayer); the worship he is performing
key_terms.عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: Mighty and Majestic; an expression of glorification for Allah
key_terms.مَلَائِكَةٌ: angels; unseen heavenly beings who serve Allah
key_terms.يَدْعُونَ: they supplicate; they ask Allah for the worshipper
key_terms.يُصَلُّونَ: they pray; here meaning they stand in prayer behind him

ai.seo_question: What happens spiritually when a Shiʿah believer stands for salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith describes the spiritual honor granted to a member of the Shiʿah when he stands for salat (prayer). It teaches that prayer is surrounded by unseen divine support, as angels gather around the worshipper and make du'a for him until he completes his prayer.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.629 - Imam Muhammad ibn Ali Al-Baqir (as) said:

"There is no servant from among our followers (Shiite) who stands for prayer except that an equal number of angels, matching those who oppose him, surround him and pray behind him, invoking Allah (swt), the Mighty and Majestic, for him until he completes his prayer."
